title: Long-term Affordability for Mental Healthcare Treatments
what_it_is: Long-term Affordability for Mental Healthcare Treatments

sections.label: Public health institution subsidies
sections.summary: Eligible patients at public health institutions can receive up to 80% subsidies for inpatient mental health treatment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: At our public health institutions (PHIs), eligible patients can receive up to 80% subsidies for inpatient mental health treatment.

sections.label: GP clinic mental health subsidies
sections.summary: Patients can receive up to $500 yearly at participating private GP clinics via the Community Health Assist Scheme for mental health conditions under the CDMP.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Patients can also enjoy subsidies of up to $500 per year at participating private general practitioner (GP) clinics via the Community Health Assist Scheme, for the management of mental health conditions under the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP).

sections.label: MediShield Life claim limits raised
sections.summary: Since 1 March 2021, MediShield Life inpatient mental health claim limits rose to $160 per day for up to 60 days per policy year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Since 1 March 2021, the MediShield Life claim limits for inpatient mental health treatment has been raised to $160 per day for up to 60 days per policy year, from the previous $100 per day for up to 35 days per policy year, which will help to improve patient affordability.

sections.label: Insurance coverage work ongoing
sections.summary: Work with insurance companies to further optimise the coverage process and ensure affordability is ongoing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: As far as working with insurance companies to further optimise the coverage process and ensure affordability, that is an on-going piece of work.

sections.label: Outcomes, withdrawal limits, taskforces
sections.summary: The principle focuses on access and affordability outcomes, setting withdrawal limits, a sustainable healthcare system, and taskforces examining infrastructure and service provisions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The principle is not so much to make sure that there is a completely flat equivalence for all conditions and for all circumstances, but what is the outcome in terms of access and affordability, both bill size, out-of-pocket and the number of incidents of care-seeking behaviour within a period of time for an individual.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, I think it is the outcome that we want to drive in terms of setting withdrawal limits, together with the outcome of a sustainable healthcare system.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: As for the provisions of infrastructure in terms of dealing with the pandemic and its effects on mental health, this is a matter that the COVID-19 Mental Wellness Taskforce is looking at, as well as the new Inter-Agency Taskforce on Mental Health.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We will be looking at the infrastructure and the service provisions that we need for our mental health needs.
